texts:
Name one product you used this morning.

How do you think it was made? Who designed, built, tested, or repaired the machines behind it?
slides.lookFor: One product plus at least one human role behind the machine.
slides.pivot: Offer phone, toothbrush, shoes, or cereal as examples; reject 'a machine' as the whole answer.

texts:
Open ClassLink → Xello → assigned work → What Is CTE?

Read the current prompt. Submit a text response or file as directed. Opening the task is not completion.

If the prompt needs more time, finish during supervised catch-up—not during Friday Matchmaker.
slides.lookFor: Every student opens the exact assigned task and submits or is recorded for catch-up.
slides.pivot: Project the teacher-demo route and current prompt; do not substitute another Xello lesson.
slides.trim: Protect the full ten minutes. Move unfinished work to supervised catch-up.

texts: Manufacturing Is More Than Assembly Lines

People in this cluster turn ideas and raw materials into finished goods.

They design, program, operate, assemble, repair, test, and improve.

Current H&L fit: Doer • Analyzer • Creator
slides.lookFor: Students replace the one-job factory stereotype with several distinct roles.
slides.pivot: Ask who programs the robot, tests the product, and keeps the line safe.

sources: Authenticated Hats & Ladders Manufacturing cluster, viewed in teacher Climber Mode on 2026-08-15.

texts:
Point to the three Hats on the opener:
Automation Specialist
Mechatronics Technician
Welder
Question: What problems might these workers solve during a normal day?
slides.lookFor: Students use the printed Hats and name a plausible problem, not only a tool.
slides.pivot: Read the opener aloud and pause after each Hat for one possible job problem.

texts:
Robotics & Automation Technology
Industrial Maintenance
Manufacturing Technology
Electronics Technology
Welding
Advanced Manufacturing & Industrial Technology

Current H&L labels

Pathways group related careers and training. A pathway is not one job.
slides.lookFor: Students can distinguish a pathway from a Hat and can locate all six current labels.
slides.pivot: Use a six-group jigsaw only if the read-aloud stalls; otherwise keep the list brief.

texts:
A welder is building a rocket launch platform.

Slow down and double-check every weld—or keep moving to meet the deadline?

Use evidence: What does the team risk in each choice?
slides.lookFor: Students name a consequence larger than the schedule, such as safety or mission failure.
slides.pivot: Ask: What does one failed weld cost compared with three extra minutes?

images.alt: Find Your Future Manufacturing opener with the welder decision-making prompt

sources: Find Your Future p. 199, Be the Decision Maker prompt.

texts:
Think silently for 30 seconds.
Partner A: 30 seconds.
Partner B: 30 seconds.

I would ____ because ____.
Slowing down costs ____, but a bad weld costs ____.
slides.lookFor: Both partners speak or use the private written route; reasons cite a tradeoff.
slides.pivot: Keep students seated if movement costs time. Call on two pairs you heard while circulating.

texts:
Clusters → Manufacturing
Open Cluster Tour
Then open Pathway Possibilities
Do not rapid-click. Use the current labels on screen.
slides.lookFor: Every student reaches Manufacturing and can see Cluster Tour plus Pathway Possibilities.
slides.pivot: Use the projected authenticated screenshot; if H&L is down, use FYF p. 212 and mark the app work pending.

texts:
Stop 1: One new career from the video
Stop 2: One question you still have

Write in the dated CCE entry:
1SW Wk1 Manufacturing
slides.lookFor: Two short notebook notes appear at the correct pauses; students do not copy the video.
slides.pivot: Pause the class video yourself if individual controls or audio create delays.

texts:
Record in the same entry:
one Manufacturing Hat that interests you
education or training
one surprising task, salary, or training detail
Salary evidence needs career, geography, measure, and date viewed.
slides.lookFor: Each student can tell you one career found and point to its current H&L profile.
slides.pivot: If a student is scrolling without a Hat, sit beside them and choose one pathway first.

texts:
Career 1 + Career 2
For each, record:
• one specific daily task
• one preparation fact
• robots, metal, or both?

Then connect one cell to your Wk0 core type.
slides.lookFor: Two different careers, one specific task and preparation fact each, plus one evidence-based core-type connection.
slides.pivot: Use the scaffolded matrix and sentence stem; accept a provisional core type if H&L access is pending.
